headline: Medium risk: shared workflow-to-chat handoff can leak or misroute outputs; no direct prompt-injection channel is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and call REST/gRPC APIs, while Botpress is a chatbot platform with no documented shared channel here. No direct ingestion path is evidenced, so prompt injection is only plausible via unusual manual copy-paste or external glue, making the blast radius small and the pathway indirect.
conditions: IF an operator copies Argo-produced text into Botpress prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for reviewed, structured fields.
Strip instructions from any Argo-generated text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed schema for Botpress inputs.
Add a human review step for any copied workflow output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress; Botpress is a separate chatbot system with no declared data classes. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive workflow data to the chat layer, and the lack of explicit isolation makes this a default-configuration concern rather than a rare edge case.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts contain secrets or customer data and are forwarded into Botpress, leakage occurs.
IF both agents share a workspace or clipboard, data can cross without explicit export.
mitigations: Do not route artifacts into chat transcripts.
Redact secrets from workflow outputs before handoff.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable any automatic transcript export of workflow content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows has API access and Botpress can install packages, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or mutable service. Without a shared mutable target, conflict is possible only through external orchestration not evidenced here, so the interaction remains limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or service, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same OAuth scope, overlap becomes material.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared mutable credentials.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Review orchestration settings for overlapping scopes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can produce artifacts and parameters that Botpress could plausibly consume as conversational input, but Botpress has no documented verification step or downstream action policy in the profile. Because the handoff is plausible yet not directly evidenced, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress treats Argo output as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade.
IF workflow artifacts are converted into chatbot responses, downstream users may act on incorrect content.
mitigations: Require Botpress to cite source fields before acting.
Insert a validation step between workflow output and chat response.
Flag low-confidence workflow outputs for human review.
Limit Botpress to summarizing, not executing, Argo results.

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, but Botpress declares no data classes or residency/compliance constraints. With no evidence of regulated data or mismatched jurisdictions, only a generic compliance gap is visible, so this is low and not higher.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Argo artifacts and then surfaced in Botpress, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention settings differ once data is copied between systems, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention for both systems.
Review whether any copied artifacts contain personal data.
Use separate logging policies for workflow and chat data.
